propositions.text: This application for judicial review challenges a visa officer’s decision dated June 28, 2018 refusing Chi Kan Kwan's permanent resident visa application.
propositions.quote: This application for judicial review challenges a visa officer’s [the Visa Officer] decision dated June 28, 2018 refusing the application of Chi Kan Kwan for a permanent resident visa as a member of the Start-up Business Class.

propositions.text: The visa officer found Ms. Kwan’s application was primarily to acquire immigration status, not to engage in authorized business activity.
propositions.quote: The stated basis for the decision was a finding that Ms. Kwan’s application for landing was primarily brought for the purpose of acquiring immigration status and not for the required purpose of engaging in an authorized business activity.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the judicial review challenges the visa officer's refusal based on finding Ms. Kwan's application was primarily for immigration status, not business.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan met initial technical requirements for the start-up business venture program, including intention to operate a business in Canada.
propositions.quote: It is common ground that Ms. Kwan’s application met the initial technical requirements to qualify as a start-up business venture under the applicable program.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan entered into an agreement with Empowered Startups Ltd., a designated business incubator in Vancouver.
propositions.quote: In Ms. Kwan’s case, an agreement was reached with a designated business incubator based in Vancouver, namely Empowered Startups Ltd.

propositions.text: The agreement described the venture as a fee-based financial website linking Chinese investors with Canadian financial institutions.
propositions.quote: The agreement described the proposed joint venture as a fee based “one stop information platform (Financial Website)” linking Chinese investors with institutions offering Canadian financial products.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Ms. Kwan met initial program requirements and had an agreement with Empowered Startups for a financial website venture.

propositions.text: A concern arose about Empowered supporting a conflicting venture, raising concerns about assisting applicants to acquire status under IRPA.
propositions.quote: The reviewing Visa Officer noted that this “raises concerns about possible [Empowered] involvement in assisting applicants in acquiring status or privilege under IRPA”.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer requested a peer review from CABI, which identified problems and noted significant changes to the business model.
propositions.quote: CABI’s peer review report dated February 16, 2018 identified problems with the proposal and noted that the business model had “changed significantly since the initial application was submitted”.

propositions.text: CABI noted Ms. Kwan committed to paying $300,000 for incubation services, which is not normal for Canadian incubators.
propositions.quote: The report also stated that Ms. Kwan “has committed to paying $300,000 for a year of incubation services. This is not normal for an incubator in Canada”.

paragraphs.summary: The Visa Officer raised concerns about Empowered's conflicting ventures and obtained a peer review noting business model changes and unusual incubation fees.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan was asked for a status update on her business establishment and operation on February 28 and March 9, 2018.
propositions.quote: On February 28, 2018, Ms. Kwan was asked to provide a status update on the establishment and operation of her business. This request was followed up with a second request on March 9, 2018.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan provided a three-page update describing a new chatbot platform business model, abandoning the initial model due to financial regulation concerns.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan then provided a three page “Venture Update” describing a new business model involving a chatbot platform connecting financial institutions with potential customers. She also explained that the initial business model had been abandoned because of financial regulation concerns.

paragraphs.summary: The Visa Officer requested updates; Ms. Kwan provided a new business model involving a chatbot platform, abandoning the initial model due to regulation concerns.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer found a lack of seriousness in Ms. Kwan’s business engagement and concluded her intentions were other than carrying out business in Canada.
propositions.quote: The lack of seriousness by PA and designated entity in entering the proposal leads me to conclude that her intentions were other than carrying out a business in Canada.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan failed to provide documentary evidence of significant progress despite claiming some successes.
propositions.quote: She indicated that her successes to date include the development of the initial website for Chatwithbanks.com and the formation of a chatbot development team, yet she has not provided any documentary evidence to support this.

propositions.text: Empowered accepted and invested in a business similar to Ms. Kwan’s initial proposal, which would compete with her business, atypical for a venture capital investor.
propositions.quote: I also note that Empowered Startups Ltd. has accepted and is investing in a business venture similar to her initial proposal which would have directly competed with her business. This is atypical of a venture capital investor.

propositions.text: Ministerial Instructions state applicants are not members of the start-up class if their commitment is primarily to acquire status, not to engage in the business activity.
propositions.quote: Item 2(5) of the Ministerial Instructions (MIs) states that an applicant is not to be considered a member of the start-up business class if they intend to participate, or have participated, in an agreement or arrangement in respect of the commitment primarily for the purpose of acquiring a status or privilege under the Act and not for the purpose of engaging in the business activity for which the commitment was intended.

paragraphs.summary: The Visa Officer found Ms. Kwan lacked seriousness, failed to show progress, and concluded her intent was to acquire status, not engage in business.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer sent a procedural fairness letter to Ms. Kwan raising concerns about the bona fides of her application and lack of progress information.
propositions.quote: The Visa Officer followed up with a procedural fairness letter to Ms. Kwan raising all of the same concerns and questioning the bona fides of her application. Included in the letter was a specific concern about the lack of information provided about the progress of the venture during the previous year.

paragraphs.summary: The Visa Officer sent a fairness letter to Ms. Kwan raising concerns about her application's bona fides and lack of progress information.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan responded with a four-page reply explaining the business model change and her work involvement.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan responded to the fairness letter in a four page reply and enclosed copies of her communications with the representatives from Empowered. Her reply explained the rationale behind the change to the business model and described the work that had gone into the new proposal.

propositions.text: She claimed about 10 hours per week engagement and said Empowered's other chatbot venture did not compete with hers.
propositions.quote: She claimed to have been actively engaged in the incubation process to the extent of “about” 10 hours of work per week. Ms. Kwan also explained that the work being done by Empowered in the development of another chatbot venture did not compete with her business idea.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan criticized the Visa Officer for second guessing and threatened legal options if decision was negative.
propositions.quote: Her letter concluded with a criticism that the Visa Officer was second guessing her business decisions and with a threat that she was exploring her legal options in the event of a negative decision.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan did not provide any documents from Empowered with her response despite their significant involvement.
propositions.quote: It is of some significance that, despite Empowered’s significant involvement in the development of Ms. Kwan’s venture, nothing from that source was provided with her response.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan replied explaining business changes, claimed active engagement, denied competition, criticized the officer, and provided no Empowered documents.

propositions.text: Despite Ms. Kwan’s answers, the Visa Officer concluded the application was primarily motivated by desire to acquire immigration status, not a legitimate business opportunity.
propositions.quote: Notwithstanding Ms. Kwan’s answers, the Visa Officer concluded that the application was primarily motivated by a desire to acquire immigration status in Canada and not to pursue a legitimate business opportunity.

paragraphs.summary: The Visa Officer concluded Ms. Kwan’s application was primarily to acquire immigration status, not to pursue a legitimate business.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer reviewed Ms. Kwan’s submissions and found insufficient evidence of active involvement in the business from within Canada.
propositions.quote: Based on the information provided by the PA, I am not satisfied that the PA has been in Canada exercising her work permit to develop her business venture. I am not satisfied that the PA will provide active and ongoing management of this business from within Canada.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan was mostly outside Canada after March 2017, with communications mainly by email and WeChat.
propositions.quote: According to the chat logs provided between the PA and Chang of Empowered Startups Ltd., the PA was no longer in Canada as of at least March 17, 2017. In her letter of explanation, the PA repeatedly indicates that the discussions about the business took place over email, WeChat call, and WeChat message.

propositions.text: Empowered representatives developed the business and website, with limited direct involvement from Ms. Kwan.
propositions.quote: The chat logs (Appendix B) suggest that Chang of Empowered Startups Ltd. was developing the PA’s business venture and providing the PA with updates. According to the April 2, 2017 e-mail between the PA and Chang (Appendix A), it appears as though Chang created the survey questions. Furthermore, Chang built the company website as per the April 21, 2017 e-mail between the PA and Chang.

propositions.text: The Collaborative Research Agreement was between UBC and Empowered, excluding Ms. Kwan and her business.
propositions.quote: Moreover, I note that the Collaborative Research Agreement was signed by UBC and Empowered (Appendix F). It did not include the PA or name her business venture.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer was not satisfied Ms. Kwan’s response disabused all concerns about her involvement and intentions.
propositions.quote: The PA’s response to my PFL was carefully considered; however, it did not satisfactorily disabuse all of my concerns.

paragraphs.summary: The Visa Officer found Ms. Kwan was mostly outside Canada, with Empowered developing the business, and her response did not allay concerns.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan challenges the reasonableness of the decision and alleges procedural unfairness.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan challenges the reasonableness of the decision and argues, as well, that it is tainted by procedural unfairness.

propositions.text: Reasonableness review applies to the first issue; correctness standard applies to the fairness issue.
propositions.quote: The first issue attracts a deferential standard of review and the fairness issue must be examined for correctness.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan challenges the decision's reasonableness and procedural fairness; court states standards of review for each issue.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan argues it was unreasonable to attribute improper purpose based solely on lack of business progress.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan asserts that it was unreasonable for the Visa Officer to attribute an improper purpose to her application based solely on a lack of progress in the development of her business.

propositions.text: This argument mischaracterizes the Visa Officer’s primary concern.
propositions.quote: This argument, however, mischaracterizes the Visa Officer’s primary concern.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan argues unreasonableness based on lack of progress alone; court finds this mischaracterizes the Visa Officer’s concern.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer doubted Ms. Kwan’s motives due to her lack of meaningful engagement and early return to Hong Kong.
propositions.quote: It was Ms. Kwan’s lack of meaningful engagement in the development of the business that led the Visa Officer to doubt her motives.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan’s minimal engagement contrasts with her stated commitment to develop the business.
propositions.quote: This history of minimal engagement stands in stark contrast to Ms. Kwan’s stated commitment to the development of her business.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Visa Officer doubted Ms. Kwan’s motives due to minimal engagement contrasting with her commitments.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan’s Commitment Certificate stated she was essential to the business as Director, primary shareholder, and CEO.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan’s Commitment Certificate stated that she was “essential” to the business and would be a Director, the primary shareholder, and the Chief Executive Officer of the company to be incorporated.

propositions.text: The Certificate described her operational role in detail and stated she would work full-time in Vancouver at Empowered’s premises.
propositions.quote: The Certificate also described Ms. Kwan’s operational role in considerable detail and stated that she would be employed in a full‑time position based in Vancouver working out of premises supplied by Empowered.

propositions.text: A work permit was requested for urgent business reasons to allow Ms. Kwan to assume employment in Canada.
propositions.quote: A work permit was also requested for “urgent business reasons” to permit Ms. Kwan to assume her employment responsibilities within Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Ms. Kwan’s Commitment Certificate detailed her essential full-time role in Vancouver and requested a work permit for urgent business reasons.

propositions.text: Empowered provided a letter supporting the project stating Ms. Kwan would attend and remain in Vancouver from January to December 2017.
propositions.quote: It is also noteworthy that Empowered provided a letter of support for the project stating that Ms. Kwan would “attend and remain located in Vancouver” between January 2017 and December 2017.

paragraphs.summary: Empowered supported the project stating Ms. Kwan would remain in Vancouver throughout 2017.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan came to Canada only one week between Feb 28 and Mar 7, 2017, then returned to Hong Kong and stayed there.
propositions.quote: Notwithstanding these assurances and the issuance of a work permit on February 25, 2017, Ms. Kwan came to Canada for only one week between the dates of February 28, 2017 and March 7, 2017 after which she returned to Hong Kong and remained there.

propositions.text: During her brief visit, she incorporated the business and met Empowered representatives twice.
propositions.quote: During her brief visit to Vancouver she incorporated the business and met twice with Empowered representatives.

propositions.text: After that visit, her involvement was limited to cursory email and WeChat exchanges with Empowered representatives.
propositions.quote: After that visit, Ms. Kwan’s active operational involvement in the business venture was limited to mostly cursory email and WeChat exchanges with representatives of Empowered.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Kwan visited Canada only briefly, incorporated the business, met Empowered twice, then had limited involvement via email and WeChat.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan reneged on her commitment to live in Vancouver and devote time to the business in Canada.
propositions.quote: This history shows that Ms. Kwan almost immediately reneged on her firm commitment to live in Vancouver and to devote her time and energy in Canada to her business.

propositions.text: She did not inform visa authorities or program officials timely about her departure or business model change.
propositions.quote: No effort was made to inform the visa authorities that Ms. Kwan had left Canada and was working from Hong Kong. Similarly, Ms. Kwan neglected to inform program officials in a timely way about the significant change that had been made to the business model.

propositions.text: This is surprising given her WeChat exchanges with Empowered and the advice she was given.
propositions.quote: All of this is surprising in the face of Ms. Kwan’s WeChat exchanges with Empowered representatives about these issues and the advice she was given (see CTR at pages 158 and 163).

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Ms. Kwan reneged on commitments, failed to inform authorities timely, despite advice from Empowered.

propositions.text: The court rejects Ms. Kwan’s argument that the Visa Officer erred by assessing motives after the application date.
propositions.quote: I reject Ms. Kwan’s argument that the Visa Officer erred by assessing her motivations at a time subsequent to the application.

propositions.text: A good faith obligation continues beyond application initiation, justifying ongoing assessment of motives.
propositions.quote: In my view, a good faith obligation continues beyond the initiation of an application under this program.

propositions.text: Commitments, progress reporting, and peer review serve a purpose only if motives are assessed beyond application date.
propositions.quote: If it were otherwise, no purpose would be served by requiring a commitment from the applicant going forward, for regular progress reporting, and for a post-application peer review.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects Ms. Kwan’s argument, stating good faith obligations and motive assessments continue beyond application initiation.

propositions.text: Nothing suggests the Visa Officer ascertained motives after application date; subsequent behaviour can assess past motives.
propositions.quote: there is nothing in the Visa Officer’s decision suggesting that Ms. Kwan’s motives were ascertained at some point subsequent to the date of her application. A person’s past motivations can be reasonably assessed by examining their subsequent behaviour and clearly that was what happened here.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan’s initial motives were questioned due to failure to live up to commitments about operational involvement.
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan’s initial motives were questioned based on her almost immediate failure to live up to the clear commitments she had given about the details of her intended operational involvement.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Visa Officer reasonably assessed Ms. Kwan’s initial motives by examining her subsequent failure to meet commitments.

propositions.text: Ministerial Instruction 7 states applicants are excluded if their commitment is primarily to acquire immigration status, not to engage in business.
propositions.quote: Ministerial Instruction 7 provides that an applicant will not be considered a member of the start-up business class “if they intend to participate, or have participated, in an agreement or arrangement in respect of a commitment primarily for the purpose of acquiring [immigration] status”.

propositions.text: This language contradicts Ms. Kwan’s argument that motive assessment is temporally limited to application date.
propositions.quote: This language belies Ms. Kwan’s argument that a temporal limitation applied to the assessment of her motives.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Ministerial Instruction 7 excludes applicants primarily seeking immigration status, contradicting Ms. Kwan’s temporal limitation argument.

propositions.text: The Visa Officer’s finding of lack of bona fide intent by Ms. Kwan was reasonable.
propositions.quote: I am satisfied that the Visa Officer’s finding of a lack of a bona fide intent on the part of Ms. Kwan was reasonable.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan failed to honour clear commitments and had minimal business activity, unlike Empowered’s active engagement.
propositions.quote: She gave clear commitments that she failed to honour and the level of her business activity was minimal at best. The problem was not that Empowered was actively engaged with the business venture but, rather the problem was that Ms. Kwan was not.

propositions.text: It was open to the Visa Officer to conclude Ms. Kwan was not serious about the business and primarily sought immigration status.
propositions.quote: On this record it was open to the Visa Officer to conclude that Ms. Kwan was not serious about the business and was instead primarily seeking immigration status.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the Visa Officer reasonably found Ms. Kwan lacked bona fide intent and was primarily seeking immigration status.

propositions.text: Visa Officer must have considered extrinsic evidence about $300,000 commitment to Empowered and had duty to inform Ms. Kwan
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan contends that the Visa Officer must have taken this extrinsic evidence into account and, therefore, had a duty to bring it to her attention.

propositions.text: Visa Officer's real reason for rejection was concern about Empowered's motivations, not Ms. Kwan's
propositions.quote: Ms. Kwan argues that the Visa Officer’s actual rationale for rejecting her application had more to do with a concern about Empowered’s motivations than hers.

propositions.text: Visa Officer's file note of Sept 12, 2017 shows concern about Empowered not fully addressed in procedural fairness letter
propositions.quote: This suspicion, she says, was also reflected in the Visa Officer’s file note of September 12, 2017 – a concern that was not fully addressed in the Visa Officer’s procedural fairness letter.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Visa Officer considered $300,000 commitment evidence and had duty to inform her; real rejection reason was concern about Empowered's motives; file note concern not addressed.

propositions.text: Visa Officer initially concerned about Empowered's business model and motives
propositions.quote: I accept Ms. Kwan’s point that the Visa Officer harboured an initial concern about Empowered’s business model and its motives.

propositions.text: Ms. Kwan was not informed about the Visa Officer's concern
propositions.quote: It is also apparent that Ms. Kwan was not told about the issue.

propositions.text: No indication Empowered's conduct was considered in rejecting Ms. Kwan's application
propositions.quote: there is nothing in the Visa Officer’s decision indicating that Empowered’s conduct was ultimately taken into account in the rejection of Ms. Kwan’s application.

propositions.text: Decision based on Ms. Kwan's lack of meaningful operational involvement, a reasonable justification
propositions.quote: The stated basis for the decision was Ms. Kwan’s lack of meaningful operational involvement with the start-up and that was, on its own, a reasonable justification for the decision.

propositions.text: No basis to conclude Visa Officer had disguised motive; explanation for Empowered's assistance accepted
propositions.quote: there is simply no basis to conclude that the Visa Officer harboured some disguised motive for the decision. Indeed, if an inference is to be drawn it would be that Ms. Kwan’s explanation for Empowered’s assistance to a similar venture was accepted and the Visa Officer’s conflict of interest concern was dispelled.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Visa Officer initially concerned about Empowered but did not consider it in decision; decision based on Ms. Kwan's lack of involvement; no disguised motive found.

propositions.text: No evidence Visa Officer's initial concerns about Empowered influenced decision, so no duty to inform Ms. Kwan
propositions.quote: In the absence of evidence that the Visa Officer’s initial concerns about Empowered were a factor in the decision, there was no requirement to bring that issue to Ms. Kwan’s attention.

propositions.text: This case differs from Sapojnikov where failure to disclose a 'poison pen' letter was a procedural fairness breach
propositions.quote: This situation is very different from the case of Sapojnikov v Canada (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship), 2017 FC 964, 285 ACWS (3d) 153, involving a failure to disclose a “poison pen” letter received one day before the sending of a procedural fairness letter.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no duty to inform Ms. Kwan absent evidence concerns influenced decision; distinguishes from Sapojnikov case involving undisclosed damaging letter.

propositions.text: In Sapojnikov, letter impugned credibility and was inferred to influence procedural fairness letter, requiring disclosure
propositions.quote: The content of the letter directly impugned the applicant’s credibility and Justice Anne Mactavish drew an inference that it must have been a factor in the decision to send the procedural fairness letter.

propositions.text: Duty to disclose evidence that influenced decision to send procedural fairness letter
propositions.quote: Accordingly, there was a duty to disclose the letter to the applicant.

paragraphs.summary: Sapojnikov case held that evidence affecting credibility and procedural fairness letter must be disclosed to applicant.

propositions.text: Visa Officer's reservations about Empowered were irrelevant to Ms. Kwan's motives or credibility
propositions.quote: In this case, the Visa Officer’s tentative reservations about Empowered had no relevance to the assessment of Ms. Kwan’s motives or her credibility.

propositions.text: CABI's reference to $300,000 commitment was not pursued by Visa Officer
propositions.quote: In fact, CABI’s reference to Ms. Kwan’s $300,000 commitment to Empowered was, not surprisingly, never taken up by the Visa Officer as a point of subsequent interest.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Visa Officer's reservations about Empowered irrelevant to Ms. Kwan's motives; $300,000 commitment not pursued by Visa Officer.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review is dismissed
propositions.quote: For the foregoing reasons, this application is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: Court dismisses the application for judicial review.

propositions.text: No certified question proposed and no issue of general importance arises
propositions.quote: Neither party proposed a certified question and no issue of general importance arises on this record.

propositions.text: Judgment is that the application is dismissed
propositions.quote: THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that this application is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes no certified question or general issue; dismisses application.
